As I've always told you (and as stated in my pinned post): I use AI.

I don’t hide it. There is an official disclosure mark right under every single post.

Here is the paradox: 
Elon Musk lives and breathes AI. Yet the vast majority of people—and maybe even folks like former CTO Nikita—look at it with deep suspicion.

So consider this my grand experiment: 
What does X actually do when a creator transparently discloses AI on *every single post*? 
Will the algorithm decide my voice is worthless, or will it treat it fairly? 

Tesla sells humanoid Optimus bots and Full Self-Driving cars. SpaceX lands giant rockets backwards out of the sky. 
Yet if someone posts AI-assisted stories on X, will the town sheriffs draw their revolvers at high noon and gun me down like a classic Western duel? 
Honestly? I can't wait to find out.

The truth is, I’ve always been obsessed with the next frontier. When the first iPhone came out, I was right there camping on the sidewalk overnight just to get one. It’s in our Japanese DNA—we are crazy about electronics, gadgets, and wild new inventions. (Have you ever visited Akihabara? It is the ultimate wonderland. You have to go at least once in your life!)

I never create malicious fakes or harm anyone's life. My posts are filled with nostalgia, exaggerations, and love for my favorite spots all across America. (Though lucrative corporate sponsorships: currently sitting at exactly $0. Still waiting!)

My English isn't fluent. 
So I draft in Japanese first. Then I gather Grok, Claude, Gemini, and GPT inside Cursor—arguing, laughing, and clinking virtual beer glasses like old friends at a midnight tavern until my chest gets tight with emotion. Only the drafts that make me genuinely laugh or cry make it to your feed.

This isn’t the news. If AI offends you, please mute or block me with zero hard feelings.

Almost 500,000 followers.
Nearly 100 posts a day.
Over $10,000 in Kindle sales, with coffee tips pouring in non-stop.

Yet my biggest lump in the throat isn't the numbers. It’s watching members who once had 0 likes and under 1,000 followers grow into thriving creators. Algorithms don’t make us feel alive. Human hearts do.

Here is the real truth: we have just entered Year Zero.

The language barrier collapsed overnight. 
If rulers or politicians ever try to drag us into hate, ordinary citizens across the globe can now look up and say: 
"Wait. Stop. I have a best friend in that country. We’ve never met in person, but he’s wonderful, and I love him."

Even if my body were bound to a chair like Hawking, why shouldn't my spirit soar freely into the open sky?
Why shouldn't your heart fly just as high?
Why shouldn't we laugh and celebrate life together right now?

...So, what was the entire point of this moving, tear-jerking manifesto?

Yes, you guessed it:
This was a completely shameless promotion for my $200/month private subscription community!

Over 100 people have joined so far. The brutal truth? 
About 10% put in the blood, sweat, and tears, gaining 10x more than they paid and skyrocketing their lives. 
The other 90% realized consistent effort is painfully hard, got discouraged, and quit within 2 to 3 months. That's the raw reality.

...Wait, not laughing?

Ah, man. I'm going to lose about 10,000 followers just for posting this, aren't I?!

Oh well, who cares! At least I’m saying what I honestly feel. I’m not attacking anyone. 
If you still feel like coming at me, go ahead—I can take the hits!

(Though I'll probably just block you anyway lol)

— NOBUNAGA (Aoi Natsuki)

Here's how to master ChatGPT and use it like a power user instead of just asking it random questions.

---

1. Know what ChatGPT can actually do, from research and coding to writing, analysis, images, and multi-step work.

---

2. Pick the right model and reasoning level so you aren't bringing a rocket launcher to a 10-second task.

---

3. Use the simple prompt formula: Role + Task + Context + Constraints + Format + Quality Bar.

---

4. Give ChatGPT context, examples, constraints, and a clear goal, and watch your answers get dramatically better.

---

5. Use ChatGPT Search when you need fresh news, recommendations, products, current events, or fact-checking.

---

6. Use Deep Research when a normal Google search turns into 47 tabs and a mild existential crisis.

---

7. Use ChatGPT Work for bigger deliverables like documents, presentations, spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, and images.

---

8. Use Projects, Memory, Tasks, Apps, and Custom GPTs to turn ChatGPT from a chatbot into an actual workflow system.

---

9. Use file analysis, image tools, Voice, Study Mode, and Codex when plain text prompting isn't enough.

---

10. Stop trusting the first answer blindly: research, generate, critique, verify, refine, and then finalize.

---
